carousels.name: 5 myths about who struggles with p*rn (JAMA 10.3% / 7.0%)

slides.title: 5 myths about [[who struggles with p*rn.]]
slides.sub: 10.3% of men and 7.0% of women reported distress from out-of-control sexual behavior.

slides.title: Men · [[7.0% women]]
slides.body: A study of 2,325 U.S. adults (Dickenson et al., JAMA Network Open, 2018) found 10.3% of men and 7.0% of women reported clinically relevant distress from trouble controlling sexual urges and behavior. For many, that struggle is p*rn.

slides.title: Myths [[1–3]]
items: "Only religious people struggle." It shows up across beliefs.
"Only single guys." People in relationships struggle too.
"Only men." Women struggle too — and talk about it even less.

slides.title: Myths [[4–5]]
items: "Only teenagers." Many adults in their 30s and 40s struggle with p*rn.
"Only weak people." P*rn is built to keep anyone watching.

slides.title: If it's [[you]]
items: Drop the stereotype — you don't have to fit one.
Talk to someone you trust.
Look for help that fits your life.
Start small: one p*rn-free day.

slides.title: 5 overrated hacks for quitting p*rn [[— and what to do instead.]]
slides.sub: Hacks help. They're just not the whole plan.

slides.title: Hacks [[1–2]]
items: Cold showers. Great for an urge. Useless for the reason you reach for p*rn.
Motivational videos. The buzz lasts an hour. The habit lasts years.

slides.title: Hacks [[3–4]]
items: A blocker alone. If you want around it, you'll find a way.
A streak counter alone. Counting days isn't changing days.

slides.title: Willpower [[sprints]]
slides.body: Going hard for a week, then crashing back to p*rn. Recovery is a marathon pace, not a sprint.

slides.title: What [[actually]] works
items: Stack them: blocker + routine + a real person.
Find your reason and keep it in sight.
Fix the trigger behind the urge, not just the urge.
Keep going after the hype wears off.
